title: Labor Commissioner wage judgments against San Francisco employers the City pays
question: Which employers with a State wage judgment against them are also paid by the City or named on City contract teams?
finding: The Labor Commissioner's judgment search lists 462 judgments from 2015 to November 2026 against defendants with a San Francisco address ($23.1 million in all; 340 open/unpaid, 68 closed-claimant judgment, 41 closed - satisfied, 10 open - partial payment/satisfaction, 1 stayed - bankruptcy, 1 stayed - other, 1 pending/open). 341 name a company; 14 of those companies match by name a City payee since fiscal 2019 or a member of a City contract team, 7 of them with the judgment still shown as open or unpaid; the largest City payee among them is Episcopal Community Services of San Francisco, Inc. ($440.8 million, judgment J-89738, $10,307).
how: The four CSV downloads (defendant city San Francisco, by date range) are combined and de-duplicated on the judgment number. A defendant is a company when its name carries a company form (Inc, LLC, LP, Corp and the like); each side of a "dba" is matched to the Controller's payment file (fiscal 2019 on) and to every supplier on a contract team in the Controller's contract file, on the project's normalised name key.
limits: A judgment is the Labor Commissioner's order after a wage claim; the search warns that payments made directly to workers are often not recorded, so "open" may be paid. Most judgments concern work for private customers, not City work. A name match can join two different firms with similar names; the City's payment files carry no address, so a match here is a name match (the Treasurer's business registry does carry addresses: the screen of wage findings under “Contractors across agencies, bids and enforcement lists” confirms some of these by street address, and for the rest the records do not show whether it is the same organization). Judgments against individuals are counted, not named.
